sehemu: Part III: Procedure, Powers and Privileges of Parliament
maudhui: (1) Subject to the other provisions of this Constitution, Parliament shall exercise its legislative power by the process of debating and passing Bills which shall ultimately require the assent of the President, and a Bill shall not become law unless it has been passed by the National Assembly and assented to by the President in accordance with this Article. (2) After a Bill is presented to the President for assent, the President may assent to it or withhold assent, and where he withholds assent he shall return the Bill to the National Assembly together with a statement of his reasons for withholding assent. (3) After a Bill has been returned to the National Assembly under this Article, it shall not be presented again to the President for assent before the expiration of six months from the date it was returned, unless at its final stage in the National Assembly before being presented again to the President the Bill is supported by not less than two-thirds of all Members of Parliament. (4) Where a Bill returned by the President is subsequently supported in the National Assembly by not less than two-thirds of all Members as provided in subarticle (3), and is presented to the President for assent for the second time before the expiration of six months from the date it was returned, the President shall assent to the Bill within twenty-one days from the date it is presented to him, failing which he shall dissolve Parliament. (5) Nothing in this Article or Article 64 shall prevent Parliament from enacting a law which delegates to any person or Government department power to make regulations having the force of law, or which gives the force of law to regulations made by any person or Government department.
